article.Citation/Title: Grabski, M., McAndrew, A., Lawn, W., Marsh, B., Raymen, L., Stevens, T., Hardy, L., Warren, F., Bloomfield, M., Borissova, A., Maschauer, E., Broomby, R., Price, R., Coathup, R., Gilhooly, D., Palmer, E., Gordon-Williams, R., Hill, R., Harris, J., ... Morgan, C. J. A. (2022). Adjunctive ketamine with relapse prevention-based psychological therapy in the treatment of alcohol use disorder. American Journal of Psychiatry, 179(2), 152-162.
article.InterventionDescription: Three weekly IV ketamine infusions (0.8 mg/kg, 40 min) or saline, each paired with mindfulness-based relapse-prevention therapy or alcohol-education control, at UK clinical research facilities.

ae_events.Description: Majority of 53 study-drug-related adverse events (in up to 20 participants across all arms) rated mild by medical staff; individual mild event types not itemized beyond the 4 rated severe.
Low mood, rated severe (significant symptoms preventing normal daily activity) by medical staff, in a participant in the active ketamine condition.
Hypertension, rated severe by medical staff, in a participant in the active ketamine condition.
Tachycardia, rated severe by medical staff, in a participant in the active ketamine condition.
Euphoria, rated severe (significant symptoms preventing normal daily activity) by medical staff, in a participant in the active ketamine condition.

article.Year: Received March 2021, published online January 11, 2022, and the version-of-record issue is 'Am J Psychiatry 2022; 179:152-162' / 'Am J Psychiatry 179:2, February 2022' — online-first and issue year agree, so no discrepancy to flag; Year=2022 per request.
article.Outcome: Co-primary outcomes were percentage days abstinent and confirmed relapse at 6 months (Methods/Primary Outcomes). No single outcome is explicitly labeled 'the' primary in a hierarchy, so precedence rule (2) applies: the abstract Results paragraph leads with, and gives the most quantitative and narrative weight to, percentage days abstinent ('there were a significantly greater number of days abstinent... in the ketamine group compared with the placebo group at 6-month follow-up'), with relapse mentioned second and reported as null. The Results section similarly opens 'Primary Outcomes' with this comparison. Value taken is the ketamine-vs-placebo (pooled across therapy conditions) intention-to-treat mean difference at 6 months: 'mean difference=10.1, 95% CI=1.1, 19.0' (Results/Primary Outcomes; also Abstract). Note: the numeral-for-equals-sign artifact ('difference510.1') recurs throughout this article (e.g., 'SD510.59', 'N581') and is read through as '=' per the instruction to resolve unambiguous punctuation/OCR artifacts; the digits themselves (10.1, 1.1, 19.0) are unaffected and reported as printed.
article.SD: No SD, SE, or test statistic is printed for this specific comparison in the main text — only the 95% CI accompanying the mean difference in the same sentence (Results/Primary Outcomes: 'mean difference=10.1, 95% CI=1.1, 19.0'). Reported as '95% CI = 1.1, 19.0' since this is the only dispersion measure given; the underlying per-arm SDs and the exact regression model output are in online supplement Table S1, which is not part of the converted text provided.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Denominator for the 6-month (24-week) percentage-days-abstinent analysis is not stated as a single number alongside the mean difference in the main text (it is in online supplement Table S1). It is derived from Figure 3's caption, which reports this same analysis's per-arm N at week 24: ketamine+therapy N=21, ketamine+psychoeducation N=22, placebo+therapy N=22, placebo+psychoeducation N=24, summing to 89 (43 ketamine-arm + 46 placebo-arm). Figure 3 is cited in the same sentence as the mean-difference statistic ('(Figure 3; see also Table S1...)'), supporting this as the correct analysis population. This differs from the N=96 randomized and N=81 who completed the trial, reflecting attrition in observed-data-only ITT analysis at the 24-week assessment.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: 13/14 described. sample_size_power coded N: the article states only that 'the study was not powered to assess an interaction between the drug and the therapy condition' (Statistical Analysis) — a caveat about one secondary/exploratory analysis, not an a priori sample-size or power justification for the primary hypotheses, and no sample-size calculation is given anywhere in the provided text (it may appear in the separately published protocol, ref. 15, not part of this converted text). All other 13 elements are explicitly described: objective (Abstract), design/setting (double-blind 4-arm phase 2 RCT at Exeter/UCL NIHR facilities), eligibility (detailed inclusion/exclusion list), intervention/comparator (ketamine/saline dosing and therapy/education protocols detailed), outcomes (co-primary and secondary outcomes listed), randomization (1:1:1:1 block design stratified by site), blinding (staff/therapist/statistician blinding described, including its limits), statistical_methods (detailed Statistical Analysis section), results (fully reported), harms (dedicated Adverse Events section), funding_coi (MRC grant and individual author COI disclosures listed).

article.BaseStatus: Coded 'Severe' from the Abstract's explicit author label ('96 patients with severe alcohol use disorder') and corroborated by the mean 7.3 (SD=2.1) DSM-5 AUD criteria endorsed (DSM-5 severe threshold is >=6 criteria).
article.Retention (%): Denominator = randomized N=96 (both randomized N=96 and screened/enrolled N=166 are reported, so randomized is used per rule). Numerator = 81, taken from the explicit statement 'Length of completed participation in the trial (from randomization to visit 10) averaged 190 days... N=81' (Results/Participant Characteristics), which is independently corroborated by summing the Figure 2 CONSORT diagram's 'completed all treatment visits' counts across arms (18+20+20+23=81). Retention = 81/96*100 = 84.4%.
article.PrimaryCare: Coded 1 because recruitment explicitly interfaced with primary care: participants were recruited 'from primary care and secondary care drug and alcohol services' (Methods/Participants, ~5% of the sample), and some were 'encouraged to undergo a supervised detoxification in primary care' before screening. This is a recruitment/referral-pathway interface only — the trial's clinical procedures themselves were delivered at dedicated NIHR research facilities, not in primary-care settings.
article.Power: Coded 1 on the bare underpowered statement: 'The study was not powered to assess an interaction between the drug and the therapy condition' (Statistical Analysis), which per the field rule counts as power having been discussed.
article.PercentFem: 35 women of 96 randomized (Results/Participant Characteristics: '96 participants (35 women...)'), corroborated by Table 1 Male N=61/96=64%. 35/96*100=36.5%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: No race or ethnicity breakdown is reported anywhere in the provided main text (Table 1 covers age, sex, site, psychiatric history, substance-use history, and DSM-5 criteria only, with no race/ethnicity row). The concept applies to this population but the information was not reported in the converted text (it may be in the online supplement, not provided). Coded '.'.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: UK trial: NIHR Exeter Clinical Research Facility and NIHR University College London Hospitals Clinical Research Facility (Methods/Participants); Discussion also references UK national ketamine-use prevalence data. Coded 'NonUS'.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0: although 95% of the sample was recruited from the general community via social media/newspaper/radio ads (i.e., not solely from specialist clinical services), the funnel involved heavy screening and exclusion (166 screened, 70 excluded — for uncontrolled hypertension, abnormal liver tests, psychiatric comorbidity, suicidal ideation, prior substance dependence, seizure history, etc.; Figure 2/Methods), and volunteer, help-seeking, abstinence-motivated participants are not representative of the broader real-world AUD treatment population.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: No income, low-income eligibility, or public-insurance criterion is described; only end-of-study remuneration 'at a level correspondent to the national living wage' is mentioned, which is compensation, not an SES-inclusion criterion. Coded 0.
article.MediatingYN: No formal mediation analysis (indirect-effect test, causal mediation model, Baron-and-Kenny sequence) is reported anywhere in the article. Coded 0.
article.ModeratingYN: Coded 1: an exploratory (not pre-specified in the original statistical analysis plan) interaction test between ketamine and therapy conditions on percentage days abstinent was run using logistic regression modeling in the ITT population ('Statistical Analysis' and 'Exploratory Analysis Outcomes' sections) — a formal interaction-term test, meeting the field's threshold. Result was non-significant at 3 and 6 months.
article.HypothesisTestReportedYN: Coded 1 per task-level adjudication: the primary comparison's 95% CI (1.1, 19.0) excludes zero, which is an inferential signal for the primary outcome, even though no explicit numeric p-value is printed for this specific ketamine-vs-placebo comparison.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: Coded 1 for the SF-12 (12-item Short Form Survey), an explicit health-related quality-of-life instrument administered as a secondary outcome (Methods/Secondary Outcomes; results noted in Results/Secondary Outcomes as 'no differences in SF-12 mental and physical health subscale scores').
article.Implementation Outcome: Coded 1: therapy-session fidelity was explicitly monitored ('an independent consultant clinical psychologist reviewed recordings on a weekly or biweekly basis to check adherence to the treatment protocol,' Methods/Therapy), which is a fidelity/implementation outcome.
article.AE_denominator: Coded 96 (all randomized participants). The severe-AE subset is explicitly stated as occurring only in the active-drug arms ('Four adverse events in three participants were rated as severe... all in the active drug condition'), which implies AE relatedness/severity assessment was applied trial-wide across both ketamine and placebo arms (otherwise this active-vs-placebo contrast for severity would not be a meaningful statement) — supporting ArmScope='pooled' and a full-sample denominator rather than a ketamine-arm-only one.

ae_events.Grabski 2022_AE01: Text states '53 adverse events in 20 participants were rated... as either definitely (N=7), probably (N=3), or possibly (N=43) related to the study drug... None... were rated as serious... and the majority were rated as mild,' with only the 4 severe events individually named. This is an aggregate, unitemized bucket for the remaining (up to 49) non-severe events; exact per-type counts and full mild-vs-any-moderate split are not given. Defaulted to Mild per the rubric's under-specified-AE rule (no signal of intervention need beyond the named severe cases) and flagged SeverityIndeterminate=Y because 'majority' does not confirm all non-severe events were mild.
ae_events.Grabski 2022_AE02: Named individually in 'Four adverse events in three participants were rated as severe (i.e., significant symptoms that prevent normal daily activity), all in the active drug condition (low mood, hypertension, tachycardia, and euphoria)' (Results/Adverse Events). No per-symptom participant count is given (4 events across 3 participants implies one overlap, not attributable to a specific symptom), so NAffected='.'. Severity taken directly from the authors' own three-tier rating scale (mild/severe used in-text) rather than the rubric, per severity-source precedence. MeetsFDASerious='N' because the same passage explicitly states 'None of these were rated as serious adverse events' — the study's 'severe' label (defined as functional impairment, roughly CTCAE Grade 2-3) is explicitly distinguished from FDA/SAE seriousness in this article's own usage.
ae_events.Grabski 2022_AE03: See AE02 rationale — same source sentence; hypertension is plausibly an acute infusion-related vital-sign change (vitals were monitored during/after each infusion) but no explicit timing is given, so Onset='unknown' rather than assumed 'in-session'.
ae_events.Grabski 2022_AE04: See AE02 rationale — same source sentence; tachycardia is plausibly acute/infusion-related but timing is not stated, so Onset='unknown'.
ae_events.Grabski 2022_AE05: See AE02 rationale — same source sentence. Flagged as a non-obvious severity call: 'euphoria' being rated 'severe' is atypical for a positively-valenced subjective effect, but the article applies its own functional-impairment-based severity definition uniformly across all four named events and explicitly confirms none met SAE criteria, so the author-assigned label is retained rather than overridden by the rubric's PAT-adaptation principle (which would otherwise tend toward Mild for an expected subjective drug effect).

config_proposal.metric: Mean difference (percentage days abstinent, %), site-adjusted intention-to-treat, ketamine vs. placebo pooled across therapy conditions at 6 months
config_proposal.note: Only a raw (non-standardized) percentage-point mean difference with a 95% CI is reported for the primary comparison (10.1, 95% CI 1.1-19.0); no per-arm SD, SE, or supported test statistic (d/g/eta_p/F/chi2/OR/RR) is given in the main text for this specific 6-month analysis (per-arm SDs are in online supplement Table S1, not provided), so no defensible conversion to Hedges' g is possible without fabricating a dispersion value. Excluded from Tier 1; routed to Tier 2 as a genuine two-arm RCT positive/significant finding of modest-to-moderate magnitude (CI excludes but is fairly close to the null on a 0-100 percentage-point scale, consistent with the authors' own 'proof-of-concept' framing).
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Significant ITT mean difference of 10.1 percentage points (95% CI 1.1, 19.0) in percentage days abstinent at 6 months, ketamine vs. placebo pooled across therapy arms, in a 4-arm double-blind RCT (N=89 analyzed at this timepoint); the co-primary relapse outcome was null (OR=0.70, 95% CI 0.28-1.75).
